title: Strict localizations above the closed point of a strict-local base change
statement:
Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], let $\bar s:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to S$ be a geometric point [def-weil-geometric-point], put $S'=S_{(\bar s)}$ [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit], and let $\bar s':\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to S'$ be its canonical closed-point lift [lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-functoriality](1). Set $X'=X\times_SS'$ with projections $p:X'\to X$ and $f':X'\to S'$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Let $\bar x':\operatorname{Spec}\Xi\to X'$ be a geometric point and let $a:\operatorname{Spec}\Xi\to\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ satisfy $f'\bar x'=\bar s'a$. Write $\bar x=p\bar x'$ and $\bar u=f\bar x$, and form the functorial maps of strict localizations [lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-functoriality](3)-(4). Then the canonical maps
$$S'_{(f'\bar x')}\longrightarrow S',\qquad S'\longrightarrow S_{(\bar u)},\qquad X'_{(\bar x')}\longrightarrow X_{(\bar x)}$$
are isomorphisms. Here the middle map is the functorial map $S'_{(f'\bar x')}\to S_{(\bar u)}$ composed with the inverse of the first map. The last isomorphism commutes with the maps to $X$ and, using $S'\cong S_{(\bar u)}$, with the maps to $S'$. In particular, for every geometric point $\bar t:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega'\to S'$, it induces an isomorphism over $X$
$$X'_{(\bar x')}\times_{S'}\operatorname{Spec}\Omega'\ \cong\ X_{(\bar x)}\times_{S_{(\bar u)}}\operatorname{Spec}\Omega',$$
where the map on the right is $\bar t$ followed by $S'\to S_{(\bar u)}$. No finiteness or properness of $f$, or algebraicity of $\Xi/\Omega$ or $\Omega'$ over its image residue field, is assumed.
